completion_conditions: A verdict with an empty checklist or an empty acceptance list is rejected by the schema, by the transport schema, and by enforce_cca_verdict with a precise reason.
An unusable generation is retried inside the same run, bounded, and a well-formed one never is.
The three suites whose fixtures encode an empty checklist are updated so each still proves the property it was written for.
The full suite, the evidence-integrity, guardian-policy, control-plane and governance-evidence suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: It happened. On PR #233 the CCA emitted a verdict with ZERO checklist entries and ZERO acceptance entries. It was caught downstream by a MergeGate rule ('CCA verdict acceptance evidence is empty'), not by the schema — the verdict was schema-VALID. `.shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json` declares checklist and acceptance as arrays with no minItems, and the transport schema the workflow passes to `--json-schema` has no minItems either, so nothing at any layer required the judge to judge anything.

The blast radius of adding minItems was MEASURED, not estimated. With `minItems: 1` on both arrays: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → 691 tests, OK. `validate_shiki` → passed. `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh` → passed (its deliberately-empty fixtures do not go through schema validation). Exactly THREE suites fail, each on a fixture that hardcodes an empty checklist: test_shiki_evidence_integrity.sh (lines 56, 267), test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh (line 434) and test_shiki_control_plane.sh (lines 280, 765, 1325). Line 280's failure is instructive: it asserts the message 'repair_required verdict must include a non-null object', and with minItems the fixture now fails for the schema reason instead, so the grep misses. Those three files are therefore in the locks, and nothing else is.

The only verdict-shaped record in the mirror with an empty checklist is `.shiki/templates/CCA_VERDICT.template.json`, which is a template rather than a mirror record and is not covered by validate_shiki's schema-conformance loop. No recorded verdict has to be rewritten.

Schema tightening alone is not enough. It converts a degenerate verdict from 'accepted' into 'the run fails', which is correct but still costs a full `gh run rerun`. And a partial `gh run rerun --failed` does NOT help: it reuses the previous job's artifact, so the stale degenerate verdict comes back. That was measured on #233 — the partial re-run reproduced the failure and only a full re-run regenerated the verdict.

The retry belongs inside the run, bounded, and only for verdicts that are UNUSABLE — absent, unparseable, or degenerate. A verdict that judged the PR and returned repair_required or needs_guardian is a real answer and must never be retried; retrying a real answer until it changes would be judge-shopping, which is exactly what a completion gate must not do.

outcome: A CCA verdict that judged nothing can no longer be emitted, accepted, or recorded, and a single unusable generation no longer costs a full manual re-run. The two are the same defect seen from both ends: the schema permits a verdict with an empty checklist, and when the model produces one there is no recovery inside the run.

Both layers matter and for different reasons: the transport schema constrains what the model is allowed to emit at generation time, and the repository schema is what every reader validates against afterwards.

Schema validation would already reject it, but its message is a generic 'array is too short' that says nothing about what the judge failed to do; the explicit check is what an operator reads on a red X.

  - `scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh` lines 280, 765 and 1325. Line 280 needs care: it asserts the message `repair_required verdict must include a non-null object`, so its fixture must become non-degenerate in order to still reach that assertion rather than failing earlier on the schema.

tasks.scope:
Add `scripts/cca_verdict_usable.py` with a pure classifier `verdict_usability(structured_output)` returning `usable`, `absent`, `unparseable` or `degenerate`, plus the reason. `degenerate` means schema-valid in shape but judging nothing — an empty checklist or an empty acceptance list. Every other value, INCLUDING a well-formed `repair_required`, `needs_guardian`, `blocked` or `insufficient_evidence`, is `usable`.

In `.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml`, insert a classification step between `Run CCA` and `Enforce CCA verdict`. When the classification is `usable`, nothing changes. When it is `absent`, `unparseable` or `degenerate`, run the CCA step once more — the same prompt, the same schema, the same allowed tools — and use the second output. Exactly one retry: a second unusable output proceeds to `Enforce CCA verdict`, which fails the job with the reason from the first task, and the retry decision is echoed into the job log so an operator can see it happened.

The retry must be reachable from `workflow_dispatch` and from `pull_request` alike, and must not change the artifact names, the evidence manifest, or the Guardian blockers comment step.

Add `tests/test_cca_verdict_usable.py` covering the classifier: absent/empty string; unparseable JSON; a degenerate verdict (empty checklist, empty acceptance, and both); a well-formed `complete`; and — this is the case that matters most — a well-formed `repair_required`, `needs_guardian`, `blocked` and `insufficient_evidence` each classified `usable`, so no real answer is ever retried. Add control-plane assertions that the workflow classifies before enforcing, retries at most once, and retries only on the three unusable classes.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: the same PR, judged three times in a row, fails three different ways. Each failure costs a full manual `gh run rerun` and the wall-clock of the whole workflow, and the operator has to know that `gh run rerun --failed` is the WRONG command here.
  Measured on PR #233: a `--failed` re-run reused the previous job's artifact and reproduced the identical stale degenerate verdict; only a full `gh run rerun` regenerated it, after which all five checks passed. So the recovery that looks cheaper is the one that cannot work, and the loop has no way to express the one that does.
  Root cause: the CCA step's output is consumed exactly once, with no classification between generation and enforcement, so an unusable generation is indistinguishable from a real negative verdict and the only recovery is outside the run.
  Why retry only the unusable classes: retrying a well-formed `repair_required` or `needs_guardian` until it changes would be judge-shopping. The classifier exists precisely to make that impossible to do by accident — a real answer of any value is `usable` and is never regenerated.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: classify the structured output, and regenerate at most once when it is absent, unparseable or degenerate.
  Reproducible when: a run whose first generation is degenerate produces a usable verdict without operator action, and a run whose first generation is a well-formed negative verdict runs the CCA step exactly once.
